page.layout: One printed page, turned sideways on the scan. Running head and page number at the top; one column of running text, with no marginal notes and no footnotes.

main_text.p: [?]turis exornavit. Obiit A. C. 1523[?], duobus relictis filiis, inter quos ita divisit imperium, ut major natu, nomine Guascar, regnum Casconicum haberet; Attahu-Alpa vero, quem corrupte Attabalibam vocant, regno Quitonis praesset. Sed cum in illa divisione incertum mansisset cuinam fratrum provincia Tho-mebamba cedere deberet, magnum pro ea inter ipsos dissidium exortum Hispanis occasionem praebuit Peruviae invadendae, quam recens detexerat Franciscus Pizarrus. Interea Attahu-Alpa fratre Guascare capto & interfecto solus imperio potitus fuit. Hujus ingentes copias facili negotio Pizantus[?] fudit, ipsumque captum, quanquam incredibilem auri & argenti vim promitteret, nefarie stran-gulavit. Ita A. C. 1533 imperium Ingarum sive Cusconicum titulô Peruviae ad Hispanos pervenit. Nam Qui post Attahu-Alpam regnarunt In-

page.notes: Scan is rotated 90 degrees; the text was read in its upright orientation. Doubtful readings: first word "[?]turis" (initial letter cut off at the edge); "1523" (the old figures are hard to read); "Pizantus" (may be "Pizarrus", since the r is hard to tell from n); "Francisçus" as printed; "Ingarum" (may be "Incarum"). The large initial Q of "Qui" is treated as an ordinary capital. The paragraph carries on from the previous page.
